name: Question 2
problem:
For the function

$$
G(s)=\frac{1}{s(s+3)},\,s>-3
$$

find the inverse Laplace transform of $G(s),$ given that
$L{{e}^{at}}=\frac{1}{s-a},\text{ }s>a.$
worked_solution:
Notice that we can write $G(s)$ as 

$$
G(s)=\frac{1}{s(s+3)}=\frac{F(s)}{s},
$$

where $F(s)=\frac{1}{s+3}.$
Also, we know that

$$
L{{e}^{at}}=\frac{1}{s-a}.
$$

Thus, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}{F(s)} & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s+3}} \\  & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-(-3)}} \\  & ={e}^{-3t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Additionally, we know that if $L{f(t)}=F(s)$, then

$$
L{{\int }_{0}^{t}f(τ)\,\text{d}τ}=\frac{F(s)}{s}.
$$

Using the property above in reverse, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}{G(s)} & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{F(s)}{s}} \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{t}f(τ)\,\text{d}τ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{t}{e}^{-3τ}\,\text{d}τ \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}{e}^{-3τ}\,{|}_{0}^{t} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(1-{e}^{-3t}).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

For the function G(s)=1s(s+3),s>−3 find the inverse Laplace transform of G(s), given that L{eat}=1s−a, s>a.

a
13(1−e−t)
b
13(e−3t−1)
c
1t+3
d
e−3t
e
13(1−e−3t)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Notice that we can write G(s) as G(s)=1s(s+3)=F(s)s, where F(s)=1s+3. Also, we know that L{eat}=1s−a. Thus, we get L−1{F(s)}=L−1{1s+3}=L−1{1s−(−3)}=e−3t.

Additionally, we know that if L{f(t)}=F(s), then L{∫0tf(τ)dτ}=F(s)s.

Using the property above in reverse, we obtain L−1{G(s)}=L−1{F(s)s}=∫0tf(τ)dτ=∫0te−3τdτ=−13e−3τ|0t=13(1−e−3t).
